value.rationale: The theorem computes a previously unreported orbit variance for every Latin square of every order from one canonical isotopy invariant, not from factorially many labelled squares. The surprising linear intercalate dependence makes variance computable by a structural count and connects recent Latin Eulerian statistics to classic subsquare theory. The zero-variance boundary is a natural, motivated consequence; the numerical checks do not carry the value assessment by themselves.
